summary: vvaharness scanned acme-billing-portal (Python/Django) end to end. Eight findings were confirmed or triaged across five vuln classes including SQL injection, unsafe deserialization, a business-logic flaw, a race condition, an information leak, a type-confusion false positive, an integer-overflow false positive, and a known-CVE dependency. The scan degraded partway through stage 2 threat modeling after a provider timeout.
degraded_reason: Stage 2 (threat modeling) provider timed out twice; proceeded with a partial threat model rather than failing the whole scan.

finding.title: SQL injection in invoice search filter
finding.impact: Full read/write access to the billing database, including stored card-reference tokens.
finding.description: The invoice search view interpolates the `q` query parameter directly into a raw SQL WHERE clause.
finding.exploit_scenario: An authenticated user sends `q=' OR '1'='1` to /billing/search and receives every tenant's invoices.
finding.recommendation: Use the ORM's parameterized filter instead of raw SQL.
finding.code_snippet: cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE note LIKE '%{q}%'")

duplicates.title: Same raw-SQL pattern in the API search endpoint
duplicates.reasoning: Identical string-interpolation call into the same db.py helper.

finding.exploitability_notes: No input validation precedes the query; reachable by any session.
finding.verdict_reason: Traced q from the view straight into cursor.execute with no sanitization.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Confirmed the WHERE clause is built via an f-string, not a bound parameter.
finding.offensive_reason: Directly reachable, no elevated role required, full data exposure.

findings.exploitability_notes: No input validation precedes the query; reachable by any session.

finding.title: Unsafe pickle deserialization of cached report payloads
finding.impact: Arbitrary code execution on the worker process that renders reports.
finding.description: Cached report payloads are loaded with pickle.loads() from a Redis key an authenticated user can influence.
finding.exploit_scenario: An attacker crafts a malicious pickle, gets it stored under their own report cache key, then triggers a re-render to execute it.
preconditions: Attacker can write to their own report cache entry.
finding.recommendation: Switch to json for the cache payload; never pickle.loads on anything not fully trusted.
finding.exploitability_notes: Cache keys are namespaced per user, so the attacker only needs their own account to control the payload.
finding.verdict_reason: Confirmed pickle.loads is reached with attacker-influenced Redis data.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Traced the cache_key back to the report_id path parameter, which is user-controlled.
finding.offensive_reason: RCE with only a low-privilege account.

findings.exploitability_notes: Cache keys are namespaced per user, so the attacker only needs their own account to control the payload.

finding.title: Discount code logic allows unlimited stacking
finding.impact: Invoices can be discounted to near-zero by repeating the same code.
finding.description: apply_discount() loops over submitted codes without checking a code was already applied to the same invoice.
finding.exploit_scenario: A user submits the same 10%-off code 20 times in one checkout request and the invoice total drops to a few cents.
finding.recommendation: Track applied codes per invoice and reject duplicates server-side, not just in the UI.
finding.code_snippet: for code in submitted_codes: total = apply_discount(total, code)
finding.exploitability_notes: Server-side loop has no dedup guard; client-side dedup is trivially bypassed by editing the request body.
finding.verdict_reason: Confirmed no server-side check against already-applied codes.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Reproduced the loop mentally against the checkout serializer; no per-code uniqueness constraint anywhere in the path.
finding.offensive_reason: Direct financial loss but no data exposure or RCE.

findings.exploitability_notes: Server-side loop has no dedup guard; client-side dedup is trivially bypassed by editing the request body.

finding.title: Internal user IDs leaked in invoice PDF metadata
finding.impact: Discloses internal numeric user IDs to any recipient of an invoice PDF.
finding.description: The PDF author metadata field is set to the raw internal user.id instead of a display name.
finding.exploit_scenario: A customer forwards their invoice PDF; anyone who inspects its metadata sees the internal user ID, useful for further enumeration attacks.
preconditions: Access to any generated invoice PDF.
finding.recommendation: Set the PDF author field to the tenant's display name, never the raw internal ID.
finding.exploitability_notes: Low severity on its own; useful only chained with an ID-enumeration path elsewhere.
finding.verdict_reason: Confirmed set_author() is called with the raw integer ID.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Inspected the PDF builder call site; no formatting layer between user.id and set_author.
finding.offensive_reason: Only useful as a reconnaissance aid for another attack.

findings.exploitability_notes: Low severity on its own; useful only chained with an ID-enumeration path elsewhere.

finding.title: Race condition in wallet balance deduction
finding.impact: Concurrent requests can deduct a wallet balance below zero, letting a customer spend funds they don't have.
finding.description: deduct_balance() reads then writes the balance without a row lock or atomic update, so two concurrent requests both pass the sufficient-funds check.
finding.exploit_scenario: An attacker fires two simultaneous purchase requests against a wallet with exactly one item's worth of balance; both succeed.
preconditions: Ability to send two concurrent authenticated requests.
finding.recommendation: Use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` or an atomic `F()` expression update instead of read-then-write.
finding.code_snippet:
balance = wallet.balance
if balance >= amount:
    wallet.balance = balance - amount
    wallet.save()
finding.exploitability_notes: Reliably reproducible by firing two requests within the same request-handling window.
finding.verdict_reason: Confirmed no row lock or atomic update between read and write.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Modeled the two-request timing window against the ORM calls; no locking primitive present.
finding.offensive_reason: Direct financial loss, moderate timing precision required.

findings.exploitability_notes: Reliably reproducible by firing two requests within the same request-handling window.

finding.title: Type confusion in webhook payload amount field
finding.impact: A string amount silently becomes 0 after a failed int() cast is caught.
finding.description: The webhook handler casts the vendor-supplied amount field with `int(amount)` inside a broad try/except that falls back to 0 on any error, rather than rejecting the payload.
finding.exploit_scenario: A malformed webhook amount field of "free" is caught and silently treated as a $0 charge instead of failing the request.
preconditions: Ability to reach the webhook endpoint (signed but replay-checked separately).
finding.recommendation: Reject the payload with a 400 instead of defaulting to 0 when the cast fails.
finding.exploitability_notes: On review, the webhook signature check happens before this handler runs, and the amount field is server-derived in practice, not attacker-controlled.
finding.verdict_reason: The upstream signature verification and payload schema check already reject non-numeric amount fields before this code runs.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Traced the call chain to webhooks/router.py and found a pydantic schema that already constrains amount to a positive int.
finding.offensive_reason: Upstream validation already closes this path in practice.

findings.exploitability_notes: On review, the webhook signature check happens before this handler runs, and the amount field is server-derived in practice, not attacker-controlled.

finding.title: Integer overflow in bulk invoice line-item total
finding.impact: A crafted line-item quantity could wrap a fixed-width total in a downstream export format, though Python ints themselves don't overflow.
finding.description: The CSV export path casts the computed total to a C-style 32-bit int for a legacy partner format before writing it out.
finding.exploit_scenario: A quantity large enough to push the computed total past 2^31-1 wraps to a negative number in the exported CSV.
preconditions: Ability to create an invoice with an extreme line-item quantity.
finding.recommendation: Validate quantity/total against the legacy format's range before export and reject or clamp instead of silently wrapping.
finding.exploitability_notes: Requires an admin-only bulk-invoice tool to create the extreme quantity in the first place; not customer-reachable.
finding.verdict_reason: The bulk-invoice tool that could set such a quantity is admin-only and already has its own range validation.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Confirmed the only caller of totals.py with attacker-influenced quantity is gated behind the admin-only bulk import tool's own validator.
finding.offensive_reason: Not reachable without admin access that already validates range.

findings.exploitability_notes: Requires an admin-only bulk-invoice tool to create the extreme quantity in the first place; not customer-reachable.

finding.title: Dependency with known CVE: Django 4.1.2
finding.impact: Inherits whatever the upstream Django advisory allows.
finding.description: requirements.txt pins Django==4.1.2, which has a published CVE fixed in a later 4.1.x release.
finding.exploit_scenario: Not independently exploitable without a code path that exercises the vulnerable Django subsystem.
preconditions: None beyond the dependency being present in the deployed image.
finding.recommendation: Bump the pin to the latest patched 4.1.x release.
finding.exploitability_notes: Informational — flagged by version match against the advisory database, not by demonstrated exploitation.
finding.verdict_reason: Version string matched against the advisory database only.
finding.verifier_reasoning: Confirmed the pinned version string against the public advisory feed for this package.
finding.offensive_reason: Exploitability depends entirely on which CVE is unpatched.

findings.exploitability_notes: Informational — flagged by version match against the advisory database, not by demonstrated exploitation.

chains.title: Injection to deserialization RCE
blocked_by_controls: WAF rule blocks common SQLi payloads on /billing/search
chains.narrative: The SQL injection (finding 1) exposes cached report keys, which the unsafe pickle deserialization (finding 2) then executes.

chains.title: Logic flaw compounds with race condition
chains.narrative: Unlimited discount stacking (finding 3) combined with the wallet race condition (finding 5) lets an attacker both zero out an invoice and double-spend the resulting wallet credit.

chains.title: Info leak aids account enumeration
blocked_by_controls: Rate limiting on /billing/search slows bulk enumeration
chains.narrative: The leaked internal user ID (finding 4) gives an attacker a seed value to target with the SQL injection (finding 1).
